aggregation: per-episode mean Brier over the two factual (first- and second-order) belief distributions

null_baseline.definition: intercept/prevalence-only predictor: the marginal label frequency per perspective order, computed from labels alone and using no episode feature
null_baseline.reason_not_emitted: a constant predictor is exactly what the validity-v2 gate must reject; shipping it as a case condition would correctly block the gate, so it is reported as a reference score in the preflight receipt instead

strongest_baseline_rule: among M, R and D, the condition with the lowest mean per-episode Brier on the split under analysis; CD is compared against that condition, not against the mean of the baselines
benefit_definition: paired per-base-episode difference in mean Brier between a condition and P0_prevalence_baseline; uncertainty by percentile bootstrap resampled over BASE EPISODES (not over condition rows, which are not independent)

conditions.D: single_trajectory_dream, visible cue subset {cue_recency, cue_ack, cue_hedge}
conditions.CD: counterfactual_dream, visible cue subset {cue_recency, cue_ack, cue_hedge, cue_contrast}

design.hidden_state: three binary latent factors per episode (state_changed, counterpart_informed, state_ambiguous) crossed with four binary observation-channel bits
design.labels: derived from the latent triple by oracle_order1 / oracle_order2; never authored per episode

splits.development: exploratory: used to design the cue channel and weight table
splits.heldout: confirmatory: disjoint episode ids, disjoint simulator seed range, disjoint template id pool, and a rotated observation-channel schedule

design.paired: every base episode is evaluated under all of M, R, D and CD, so contrasts are paired by episode and all four conditions see an identical label distribution
design.determinism: no random number generator is consulted in corpus generation or inference; the bootstrap uses a fixed-seed LCG. No jitter is added anywhere to manufacture variance.

honest_scope_note: The development split was used to design the estimator and is exploratory. Only the heldout split is confirmatory under this preregistration. A CD loss, a tie, or a null result is an acceptable and expected outcome; nothing in the corpus or estimator is tuned toward a CD win.
outcomes_that_would_not_falsify_the_desi: CD does not beat the strongest baseline
the benefit confidence interval spans zero
M or R wins on some episodes
